answer: The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the kernel funding graph is rebuilt from the anchor history every epoch. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 189 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator forfeits 189 bonds yet holds one position, and the cipher report publishes the merged exposure. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
